title: Two Pointers & Sliding Window
summary: Use **two pointers** to move through related positions. Use a **sliding window** when a contiguous group grows and shrinks.
refresher: **Two pointers** track two positions, often left and right. A **sliding window** tracks a contiguous range and updates a running value as the range grows or shrinks.

advanced-tp-purpose.title: Two pointers avoid extra scanning
advanced-tp-purpose.body: **Two pointers** let you move from both ends or keep two related positions.
advanced-tp-purpose.example: left starts at 0, right starts at n - 1
advanced-tp-purpose.notice: The movement rule is the whole solution.
advanced-tp-purpose.mistake: Moving both **pointers** every time can skip valid answers.

advanced-window-meaning.title: A window is a current slice
advanced-window-meaning.body: A **sliding window** is the group between left and right.
advanced-window-meaning.notice: When the window changes, update the stored sum/count too.
advanced-window-meaning.mistake: Shrinking the window without subtracting the removed **value** **leaves** stale data.

sections.title: Two pointers
sections.summary: Two positions move with a rule.

blocks.body: Two-**pointer** problems usually become easier when you name what each pointer means. In a sorted two-sum problem, left points at a small **value** and right points at a large value.

blocks.caption: Sorted two-sum moves one **pointer** based on the sum.

blocks.title: Movement rule
items: If the sum is too small, move left rightward to get a larger **value**.
If the sum is too large, move right leftward to get a smaller **value**.
Do not move both unless the logic proves both are safe to discard.

blocks.prompt: In a sorted **list**, the pair sum is too small. Which **pointer** usually moves?
blocks.why: Moving left rightward can increase the sum.

sections.title: Sliding window
sections.summary: A window is a contiguous part of the **input**.

blocks.body: A **sliding window** keeps a current range from `left` to `right`. As `right` grows, the window includes more items. When the window breaks a rule, `left` moves forward until the rule is fixed.

blocks.caption: Longest subarray with sum at most limit, assuming nonnegative numbers.

python.code:
def longest_at_most(nums, limit):
    left = 0
    total = 0
    best = 0
    for right in range(len(nums)):
        total += nums[right]
        while total > limit:
            total -= nums[left]
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best

blocks.title: Read the window code
items: Add the new right **value** to the total.
While the rule is broken, subtract the left **value** and move left.
After the rule is fixed, update the best answer.
The window is always the **values** from left through right.

blocks.title: Sliding window needs the right kind of data
blocks.body: The sum example assumes nonnegative numbers. Negative numbers can make the window shrink/grow logic unreliable.

sections.title: Trace the window
sections.summary: Write left, right, total, and best.

blocks.title: Trace [2, 1, 4] with limit 5
items: remove nums[left]=2, left becomes 1, total=5, window=[1,4], best stays 2.

blocks.caption: Keep window state updated.
blocks.body: The stored total must match the actual window.

blocks.prompt: What should happen before keeping a new **value** that makes the window too large?
choices: Shrink from the left until valid
blocks.why: A **sliding window** fixes the broken rule by moving the left side.

blocks.body: An invariant is a rule that stays true while the algorithm runs. For a window problem, write the invariant in plain English: `total is the sum of nums[left] through nums[right] and total is at most limit after the while loop`.

blocks.title: Plain-English invariant
blocks.body: You do not need fancy wording. Just say what your **pointers** mean and when they are allowed to move.
